full_story_part2_c1.parent_text: For an hour, he sat listening while I stood completely still. Finally, he groaned softly in fear, not pain. I knew that sound well. I opened the lantern's cover, sending light onto his eye. It was completely open now. I heard low, quick beats, like a watch wrapped in cotton. His heart grew faster and louder—what if a neighbour heard? I rushed at him, and he gave one scream. I pulled him down and covered him with the heavy bed. Finally his heart stopped, and I could feel no pulse. I hid his body under three floorboards, then replaced them exactly. You could search all night and find no mark. At four that morning, three police officers arrived and knocked. A neighbour had heard a scream from the house.

full_story_part3_c1.parent_text: I welcomed them and blamed my scream on a bad dream. I said the old man was away in the country. After showing every room, I brought chairs into his bedroom. You see, I sat right above the body without fear. They talked in a friendly way while I smiled. My head started hurting, and I heard a ringing sound. No—it was that low, quick beating once again. I raised my voice, but the beating grew louder too. I walked about and scraped my chair across the floorboards. They went on talking and smiling as before. The sound kept growing louder and louder! Could you bear that? They heard and knew—they were laughing at me! I could not stand any more. "I killed him!" I screamed. "Pull up the floorboards here! That is the beating of his horrible heart!"
